fd_0001.says: Young green garden pod shelled fresh in spring and eaten sweet
fd_0001.why: It is a dried or fresh-shelled cowpea, starchy and earthy, not a sweet green garden pea.

fd_0002.says: Boneless chicken breast marinated in buttermilk and cooked crisp
fd_0002.why: The name is the method. The meat is usually beef steak, sometimes pork, cooked the way chicken is.

fd_0003.says: Stir-fried Chinese noodles tossed with soy sauce and vegetables
fd_0003.why: It is a jarred vinegar relish from the American South, not a noodle dish.

fd_0004.says: Hot braised red cabbage, stewed soft with apple and vinegar
fd_0004.why: It is raw cabbage dressed cold, crisp and crunchy, not cooked soft.

fd_0006.says: Fluffy wheat-flour pancakes stacked high and served with syrup
fd_0006.why: They are thin and cornmeal-based, crisp at the edge, closer to a corn griddle bread.

fd_0007.says: Fresh sweet corn cut from the cob and simmered in butter and cream
fd_0007.why: It is dried field corn treated with alkali, starchy and chewy, not fresh sweet corn.

fd_0008.says: Spicy Creole rice cooked with sausage, shrimp and tomatoes
fd_0008.why: That is jambalaya. This one is plainer: rice, field peas and smoked pork.

fd_0009.says: Sweet, perfumed white grape grown for Mediterranean dessert wines
fd_0009.why: That describes muscat. This is a separate American grape species with a thick, tough skin.

fd_0011.says: Dark, bitter syrup left over from refining sugarcane into white sugar
fd_0011.why: That is molasses, a sugar byproduct. This is the whole juice of a different plant, boiled down.

fd_0012.says: Thick, creamy sauce of crumbled sausage drippings, flour and milk
fd_0012.why: That is sausage sauce for biscuits. This one is thin ham drippings lifted with coffee.

fd_0014.says: Tender young spinach leaves wilted quickly in butter and fresh garlic
fd_0014.why: These are tough cabbage-family leaves that need a long, slow braise to soften.

fd_0015.says: Unaged corn whiskey made at home in the Southern hills
fd_0015.why: The word is Southern for liquor in the old sense of liquid. It is cooking broth, not a spirit.

fd_0016.says: Wild legume foraged from pasture edges, not a crop anyone plants
fd_0016.why: They are a planted summer crop of cowpeas. The name means farm peas as against garden peas.

fd_0017.says: Tiny Lowcountry mustard seed, ground hot for pickles and relish
fd_0017.why: It is sesame, a mild nutty seed toasted for crunch, not a hot mustard seed.

fd_0018.says: Everyday white long grain tinted yellow with saffron or turmeric
fd_0018.why: The gold is the color of the hull in the field. The milled grain is white.

fd_0019.says: Soft Spanish sheep's milk spread seasoned with smoked paprika
fd_0019.why: It is American cheddar with mayonnaise and mild sweet peppers, with no smoky paprika.

fd_0022.says: Small green chili pepper, pickled whole and served for its heat
fd_0022.why: It is a mild seed pod with no heat, though it is often pickled alongside chilies.

fd_0023.says: Roasted groundnuts glazed with sugar and salt, served warm
fd_0023.why: They are boiled soft in salted water, never roasted, and eat like a tender bean.

fd_0024.says: Thick red chili mash, fermented and aged for years in oak barrels
fd_0024.why: It is a quick steep of whole peppers in vinegar, thin and clear, not a fermented mash.

fd_0025.says: Cooked at a hard bubble, which makes tough meat more tender
fd_0025.why: A hard boil tightens and toughens meat. Tenderness comes from gentle, long heat.

fd_0027.says: Soaked in vinegar so the meat turns tangy and sour before cooking
fd_0027.why: A brine is salt and water. It seasons the meat without making it sour.

fd_0028.says: Tossed in a store-bought caramel sauce once the food is fully cooked
fd_0028.why: Caramelizing is sugar browning in the pan as the food cooks, not a sauce poured on after.

fd_0030.says: Always smoked over wood, which is what keeps the meat from spoiling
fd_0030.why: Salt does the curing. Smoke is optional flavor, and many cured meats are never smoked.

fd_0031.says: Cooked in fairly cool oil, which keeps the food from turning greasy
fd_0031.why: Oil that is too cool soaks in. Hot oil crisps the surface fast and leaves less grease.

fd_0033.says: Left for months in a crock to sour, so it can never be made quickly
fd_0033.why: Quick pickles turn sour in vinegar within hours, and long fermenting is only one way to pickle.

fd_0035.says: Treated with chemical additives so it lasts on a shelf for years
fd_0035.why: On a menu it means methods like salt, sugar, acid or drying, not a lab process.

fd_0036.says: Chopped very finely by hand into tiny, even, crunchy cubes
fd_0036.why: It is blended or sieved completely smooth, with no pieces at all.

fd_0038.says: Cooked slowly over low heat until soft and pale, never browned
fd_0038.why: It uses high heat for speed, and light browning is part of the point.

fd_0039.says: Browned quickly over high heat to seal the juices inside the meat
fd_0039.why: Searing does not seal in juices: a seared steak loses as much moisture as an unseared one, or more.

fd_0041.says: Brushed with a bottled flavoring and a rub, then baked quickly in an oven
fd_0041.why: It takes its flavor from smoldering wood itself, not from a bottle and an oven.

fd_0042.says: Sealed in plastic and steamed until it is cooked all the way through
fd_0042.why: The bag is held in a water bath at its exact doneness, not steamed until cooked through.

fd_0044.says: Soaked in lemon water or cold milk to turn it paler before it is served
fd_0044.why: The name means to whiten, but it is a quick dip in boiling water, not a bleaching soak.

fd_0046.says: Cooked slowly over very low heat for several days until it turns sour
fd_0046.why: Microbes make the sour flavor over time; cooking heat would kill them, not sour the food.

fd_0047.says: Trimmed of every last bit of fat before cooking so that it eats lean
fd_0047.why: The fat is melted out in the pan, and the skin stays on to turn crisp.

fd_0048.says: Charred over a roaring open flame until the skin turns burnt and bitter
fd_0048.why: It is seared in a hot skillet, and the dark crust is toasted spice, not burnt char.

fd_0050.says: Small sea snails picked from the shell and served chilled with lemon
fd_0050.why: These are land snails, and the dish is served piping hot in butter, not cold.

fd_0051.says: Wild game bird shot in season, every bit as dark and strong as venison
fd_0051.why: It is a farmed bird, and its meat is only a shade darker and richer than chicken.

fd_0052.says: Tiny wild-shot bird with a strong, gamy flavor and dark, livery meat
fd_0052.why: Restaurant quail is farmed and eats mild, only a little richer than chicken dark meat.

fd_0053.says: Wild city pigeon trapped in season, stringy and strongly flavored
fd_0053.why: It is a farm-raised young pigeon taken before it ever flies, so it is tender.

fd_0054.says: Calf testicles, sliced thin, breaded and fried until crisp
fd_0054.why: Those are mountain oysters. Sweetbreads are the thymus or pancreas gland.

fd_0054.says: Sweet yeast dough fried in lard and rolled in cinnamon sugar
fd_0054.why: It is not bread or pastry at all but a gland, most often from veal.

fd_0055.says: Liver of wild ducks taken in season, naturally richer in autumn
fd_0055.why: It comes from farmed ducks or geese, force-fed in their last weeks, not wild birds.

fd_0056.says: White meat from the bird's chest that must always be served well done
fd_0056.why: It is red meat, and most kitchens serve it pink and sliced like a steak.

fd_0057.says: Older laying hen, slow-stewed for hours because the meat has grown tough
fd_0057.why: It is the opposite: a chicken taken very young, tender enough to roast fast.

fd_0058.says: Dark, gamy meat of a wild hare, hung for days before it is cooked
fd_0058.why: Menu rabbit is a farmed domestic animal with pale, mild meat, not dark, hung wild hare.

fd_0059.says: Well-marbled meat of wild boar, roasted slowly like a pork shoulder
fd_0059.why: Venison is deer, not boar, and it is very lean rather than marbled.

fd_0063.says: Gristly, strong-tasting organ that stays chewy however long it cooks
fd_0063.why: It is a muscle that turns tender with long cooking and tastes like mild roast beef.

fd_0064.says: Soft Louisiana sausage of pork, rice and liver, squeezed from its casing
fd_0064.why: That is boudin. This one is chunked pork, firm and smoked, sliced into coins.

fd_0065.says: Spicy pork sausage colored red with tomato and cayenne, always sold raw
fd_0065.why: The red comes from paprika or dried chiles, and the Spanish kind is dry-cured, not fresh.

fd_0066.says: Italian sausage of ground pork neck, fermented and dried in a casing
fd_0066.why: It is one whole muscle cured intact, not ground meat, even though it dries in a casing.

fd_0067.says: Pork leg soaked in a sweet brine, then baked and glazed until moist
fd_0067.why: That describes the wet-cured city style. This one is rubbed with dry salt and aged, never soaked in brine.

fd_0068.says: Italian pork jowl, heavily smoked like bacon, then diced into pasta
fd_0068.why: It is cured and air-dried without smoke, which is what sets it apart from bacon.

fd_0069.says: Rendered pork fat, melted and strained, used for frying and pastry
fd_0069.why: That is lard. This is a solid slab of back fat, cured and sliced, never melted down.

fd_0070.says: Cured pork tenderloin from Spain, the small soft muscle under the spine
fd_0070.why: It is the loin, the large muscle along the back. In Spain the tenderloin is called solomillo.

fd_0071.says: Italian dry-cured pork leg, diced small and crisped for pasta sauces
fd_0071.why: It is the belly, not the leg. A dry-cured pork leg is a ham, such as prosciutto.

fd_0072.says: Brined beef that is only smoked, then dried and sliced cold like a ham
fd_0072.why: Smoke is not the last step: it is steamed for hours until tender and usually served warm.

fd_0072.says: Beef rubbed with pepper and oven roasted, with no brine and no smoke
fd_0072.why: That is roast beef. The days in brine and the smoke are what make it what it is.

fd_0073.says: Smooth paste of pure liver, always made with no other meat or fat
fd_0073.why: Liver is common but not required, and most are built on pork and fat with other meats.

fd_0074.says: Italian pork leg, smoked over beechwood and cooked before slicing
fd_0074.why: The crudo style taught here is never smoked or cooked: salt, air and time do the work.

fd_0076.says: Smoked Alpine pork leg, fully cooked and carved thick like deli ham
fd_0076.why: It is never cooked: it is cured, cold smoked and aged, then sliced thin and eaten as it is.

fd_0077.says: Mild, sweet ham from the pork hind leg, carved thick as a main course
fd_0077.why: It is spicy shoulder, not leg, and it seasons a dish in small dice instead of being carved.

fd_0078.says: Any shared board of cheese, fruit, nuts and crackers, with or without meat
fd_0078.why: The word means prepared meats. A board with no cured meat is a cheese or snack board.

fd_0079.says: Lean pork loin from the Italian Alps, salt-cured and air-dried firm
fd_0079.why: It is beef, which is why it is the lean, dark red meat on a board that is mostly pork.

fd_0081.says: Calabrian chili paste made with olive oil, with no meat in it at all
fd_0081.why: It is a cured pork salami first. The chili is a seasoning, and the softness comes from pork fat.

fd_0082.says: Everyday Spanish ham from white pigs, dried in mountain air for a year
fd_0082.why: That describes serrano. This ham comes from Iberian-breed pigs and ages far longer.

fd_0082.says: Spanish ham heavily smoked over oak, then cooked and sliced thick
fd_0082.why: It is never smoked or cooked, only salted and air-dried, and it is carved very thin.

fd_0084.says: Deep lidded bowl for serving soup, and the hot soup ladled out of it
fd_0084.why: That is a tureen. This is a cold, sliced loaf named for the mold it is baked in.

fd_0085.says: Brisket slow-cooked with sweet corn kernels, an Irish American classic
fd_0085.why: Corn here is an old word for the coarse grains of salt used in the cure, not the vegetable.

fd_0086.says: Thick layer of outside fat trimmed from the top of a beef rib roast
fd_0086.why: It is a muscle, not a fat layer, and it is the most prized meat on the steak.

fd_0087.says: Lean, naturally soft muscle from the face that cooks quickly like a steak
fd_0087.why: It is tough and full of connective tissue, and only hours of braising make it soft.

fd_0089.says: The pig's foot below the ankle, all skin and small bones, pickled or stewed
fd_0089.why: That is the trotter. This is the joint just above it, where the leg meets the foot.

fd_0090.says: The strips of meat from between the bones of a rack of barbecue ribs
fd_0090.why: It is the large muscle lying on top of the rib bones, not the meat between them.

fd_0091.says: Tender, lightly worked roast above the front leg needing only a quick sear
fd_0091.why: It works hard and is tough until long, slow cooking melts its connective tissue.

fd_0092.says: Beef from the brisket, the breast muscle, sold on a small piece of bone
fd_0092.why: It comes from the lower rib cage in the chuck and plate, next to the brisket but not part of it.

fd_0093.says: The wide, lean roast along the back of a pig that chops are cut from
fd_0093.why: That is the loin. The tenderloin is the small tapered muscle tucked beneath it.

fd_0094.says: The pig's stomach lining, an organ meat simmered for hours until it turns soft
fd_0094.why: It is muscle and fat from the underside of the animal, not the stomach or any organ.

fd_0095.says: A thin, lean steak sliced from the round, the hard-working back leg
fd_0095.why: It comes from the short loin along the back, a tender area, not from the leg.

fd_0096.says: Two regional names for exactly the same steak, identical in size and makeup
fd_0096.why: They differ in how much tenderloin they carry: the porterhouse has the wider piece.

fd_0096.says: A steak pairing ribeye and tenderloin on either side of one central rib
fd_0096.why: The large side is strip loin, not ribeye, and the cut comes from the short loin, behind the ribs.

fd_0100.says: A thin steak pounded out with a mallet and seared under a heavy press
fd_0100.why: The name describes the shape of the muscle, not a way of pounding or pressing it.

fd_0101.says: A style of slow smoked barbecue, not any particular part of the animal
fd_0101.why: It is a specific cut, the chest of the steer, and it is braised and cured as well as smoked.

fd_0103.says: The upper thigh of the animal, lean and tender enough to grill as a steak
fd_0103.why: It is the lower leg, the shin, and it is far too sinewy to grill. It needs hours of braising.

fd_0104.says: A lean steak from the hind leg that has to be braised to turn tender
fd_0104.why: It comes from the sirloin, not the leg, and it is tender enough to grill or roast.

fd_0105.says: The belly ribs of a young sheep, slow-smoked like barbecue spare ribs
fd_0105.why: It is the upper ribs with the tender loin eye attached, roasted fast and served pink.

fd_0106.says: A loin slice from the hog that is only ever served well done, never pink
fd_0106.why: Since 2011 the national guidance has been 63 C (145 F) with a rest, and many kitchens serve a blush of pink.

fd_0106.says: A thick slice of the hog's hind leg, cured and smoked before it is grilled
fd_0106.why: That is a ham steak. This cut is fresh meat from the loin along the back, not cured leg.

fd_0107.says: Beef from cattle massaged daily and fed beer to make the meat tender
fd_0107.why: That is mostly legend. The marbling comes from breeding and long, careful feeding.

fd_0107.says: A protected name for beef raised only around the city of Kobe
fd_0107.why: That describes Kobe, one regional brand. The word covers the Japanese breeds wherever they are raised.

fd_0108.says: Lean, white-fleshed relative of cod from polar seas, with large mild flakes
fd_0108.why: It belongs to the salmon family, and its flesh is pink and fairly rich, not white and lean.

fd_0109.says: Small saltwater shrimp from the Gulf, sold under a Louisiana nickname
fd_0109.why: It lives in fresh water and is built like a lobster, with claws, not like a shrimp.

fd_0110.says: Dense, meaty steak cut from a small shark and grilled like swordfish
fd_0110.why: It is the thin, ribbed wing of a ray, soft and stranded, and nothing like a dense steak.

fd_0111.says: Flatfish with both eyes always on its left side and firm, meaty flesh
fd_0111.why: Some flounders are left-eyed and some right-eyed, and the flesh is delicate, not firm.

fd_0113.says: Rich, oily white fish whose silky flesh stays moist however long it cooks
fd_0113.why: It is one of the leanest fish on a menu and dries out quickly when overcooked.

fd_0114.says: Round, sandy bivalve that is saltier and chewier than a clam, served raw
fd_0114.why: They are softer and sweeter than clams, and they are served cooked, not raw.

fd_0115.says: The shellfish that jewelry pearls are taken from, eaten raw on the half shell
fd_0115.why: Pearl oysters are a different family, and the eating kind almost never makes a pearl of any value.

fd_0116.says: Soft white sacs from a male fish, pan-fried in butter and lemon
fd_0116.why: That is milt, from the male fish. These are the eggs of the female.

fd_0117.says: Naturally pale white fish whose farmed flesh is dyed pink at packing
fd_0117.why: The color comes from a pigment in the diet, krill in the wild and added to feed on farms.

fd_0118.says: Rounds punched out of skate or shark wings and sold as shellfish
fd_0118.why: A long-running myth. They are the real muscle of the shellfish, cut from the shell.

fd_0120.says: Delicate, flaky white fish that falls apart like cod when cooked
fd_0120.why: Its flesh is dense and meaty with almost no flake, and holds together like a chop.

fd_0121.says: Lean, sweet-tasting fish usually caught in shallow water near shore
fd_0121.why: It lives deep, at the edge of the continental shelf, often hundreds of feet down.

fd_0122.says: Strong-tasting oily sea fish with dark flesh, much like mackerel
fd_0122.why: Farmed rainbow trout is a mild, lean freshwater fish with pale, tender flesh.

fd_0124.says: Small shallow-reef fish farmed in pens off the Keys, soft and oily
fd_0124.why: It lives in deep water far offshore, is caught wild on hook and line, and is lean and firm.

fd_0125.says: Salt-cured eggs of wild sturgeon, netted today in the Caspian Sea
fd_0125.why: Almost all caviar sold now is farmed. Wild Caspian sturgeon were overfished and are protected.

fd_0126.says: Salted anchovy fillets mashed into a paste and melted into sauces
fd_0126.why: It is a whole dried roe sac, shaved or grated, not a paste made from fillets.

fd_0128.says: Rich, oily deep-water fish from the Southern Ocean, in thick fillets
fd_0128.why: That is Chilean sea bass, a different fish. This one is small, lean and from the Atlantic.

fd_0129.says: Lean, delicate freshwater fish that flakes apart at a gentle touch
fd_0129.why: It is a saltwater fish, rich for a white fish, and firm enough to grill.

fd_0130.says: Delicate flaky white fish, best poached gently and eaten with a spoon
fd_0130.why: It is one of the densest, firmest fish on the menu and is usually grilled.

fd_0131.says: Pale, flaky white fish that is always cooked through before serving
fd_0131.why: The fresh fish is deep red and usually served raw or rare. Only albacore is pale.

fd_0132.says: Imitation shellfish meat made from minced white fish pressed into shape
fd_0132.why: It is a real whole fish, and the tail is cut straight from it.

fd_0133.says: Young of a bigger crustacean, caught before it grows to full size
fd_0133.why: Shrimp never grow into prawns, and prawn is often just another market name.

fd_0134.says: Cold-water giant from Alaska, sold as frozen precooked legs
fd_0134.why: That is king crab. This is a small East Coast swimmer picked for its body meat.

fd_0135.says: Separate species of tiny sea creature, eaten whole from birth
fd_0135.why: It is an ordinary blue crab caught in the few hours after it molts.

fd_0136.says: Warm-water crustacean with no claws, sold mostly as frozen tails
fd_0136.why: That is spiny lobster. This one lives in cold water and carries two big claws.

fd_0137.says: Shellfish that must always be cooked and is never eaten raw
fd_0137.why: Small hard clams like littlenecks are a raw bar staple on the half shell.

fd_0138.says: Thin slices of sea snail, cut and dressed to look like a mushroom
fd_0138.why: It is a cultivated mushroom. Only the name and the chewy texture come from the sea snail.

fd_0140.says: Wild funnel named for its poison, eaten only after a long boil
fd_0140.why: The death in its French name is for its dark color and season, not poison. It cooks in minutes.

fd_0141.says: Pale farmed mushroom that only turns golden once browned in butter
fd_0141.why: It is golden when raw, and it is foraged in the wild, not farmed.

fd_0143.says: Mushroom whose small cap is eaten and whose thick stem goes to stock
fd_0143.why: The thick stem is the best part, firm and meaty, and it is what cooks slice and sear.

fd_0144.says: Delicate spring mushroom usually sliced raw into salads
fd_0144.why: Morels must be cooked through. Raw or undercooked, they can make people ill.

fd_0145.says: Mushroom that tastes briny, like the shellfish it is named for
fd_0145.why: The name is for its shell-like shape. The flavor is mild and earthy, not of the sea.

fd_0146.says: Soft, spongy mushroom with a mild, almost neutral woodsy flavor
fd_0146.why: The cap is firm and meaty, and its flavor is strongly savory and smoky, not mild.

fd_0147.says: Knobby black mushroom that grows on the bark of old oak trees
fd_0147.why: It grows underground on the roots, never on bark, and is found by smell, usually by a trained dog.

fd_0148.says: Rich pressing made by crushing whole black truffles like olives
fd_0148.why: Truffles hold almost no fat, and nearly all such bottles are flavored with a made compound.

fd_0149.says: Young Italian truffle dug from under oak roots before it ripens
fd_0149.why: It is an above-ground mushroom with a cap, a thick stem and pores, not a truffle at any age.

fd_0150.says: Small white mushroom, the pale everyday kind sold in every grocery
fd_0150.why: That is the white button. This is its brown strain, a little firmer and more flavorful.

fd_0152.says: Seaweed-like fungus with a natural briny taste of the sea
fd_0152.why: Its flavor is mild and faintly sweet. The seafood likeness is the shredded texture, not a sea taste.

fd_0153.says: Farmed mushroom grown on poultry manure, named for how it is raised
fd_0153.why: It is wild, grows on tree trunks, and the name comes from its chicken-like texture.

fd_0154.says: Name of one protected cheese made in a single French village
fd_0154.why: It is a milk word meaning ewe and covers many cheeses, fresh and aged.

fd_0155.says: Rich, high-fat cream left behind after butter is churned
fd_0155.why: It is low in fat. Churning takes the fat into the butter and leaves a thin liquid.

fd_0156.says: Soft goat cheese whose tang comes from lemon juice mixed in
fd_0156.why: The tang comes from cultures souring the milk, not from added lemon juice.

fd_0157.says: Plain sweet cream, fresh from the dairy, never soured
fd_0157.why: Despite the name it is cultured cream with a tang, not plain fresh cream.

fd_0159.says: Hard grating cheese whose crunchy white specks are grains of salt
fd_0159.why: The crunchy specks are clusters of an amino acid, tyrosine, formed during long aging.

fd_0161.says: Butter blended with ground roasted hazelnuts into a warm sauce
fd_0161.why: The name describes its color and hazelnut smell, not a blend with ground nuts.

fd_0162.says: Plain melted butter, kept warm in a small pot for dipping
fd_0162.why: It is cooked until the solids toast and then strained, which plain melted butter never is.

fd_0163.says: Butter blended with oil so it can take high heat without burning
fd_0163.why: It is butter mixed with flavorings and served cold on hot food, not a cooking fat.

fd_0164.says: Sweetened whipped cream folded with egg yolks for dessert
fd_0164.why: It is a set cream cheese on its own. Tiramisu adds the egg and sugar to it.

fd_0165.says: The Italian name for cottage cheese, the same curds sold in tubs
fd_0165.why: Cottage cheese is curds of milk, while this is traditionally made by reheating whey.

fd_0166.says: A ball of mozzarella aged until its center turns soft and runny
fd_0166.why: The center is a separate filling of cream and curd, and it is eaten fresh, never aged.

fd_0167.says: Firm, low-moisture block made for shredding and melting on pizza
fd_0167.why: That is the drier, packaged style. This one is soft, wet and sold in liquid.

fd_0170.says: Soft cheese with a white wax coat that is peeled off before eating
fd_0170.why: The white skin is living mold grown on the cheese, and it is meant to be eaten.

fd_0171.says: Aged cheese rinsed in fresh water to mellow it into a clean, mild taste
fd_0171.why: It is washed in brine, sometimes with alcohol, and that makes the rind stronger and more pungent.

fd_0172.says: Large baked tubes of dried pasta, stuffed with ricotta and spinach
fd_0172.why: They are small pinched pockets of fresh egg pasta, boiled rather than baked.

fd_0173.says: A dark variety of rye, ground coarse for a sour, malty taste
fd_0173.why: It is not rye or any grass; it is the seed of a plant in the rhubarb family.

fd_0174.says: Raw cracked wheat that needs an hour of simmering to soften
fd_0174.why: It is cooked before it is cracked, so a soak or a few minutes of simmering is enough.

fd_0175.says: A heritage variety of barley with a big, chewy, nutty grain
fd_0175.why: It is a hulled wheat, most often emmer, not a barley.

fd_0176.says: A modern hybrid of wheat and rye, bred for a tiny, tender kernel
fd_0176.why: It is one of the first farmed wheats, not a modern cross, and nothing to do with rye.

fd_0178.says: Coarse cracked wheat simmered in milk into a breakfast porridge
fd_0178.why: It is made from ground dried corn, not wheat, so it tastes of corn.

fd_0180.says: Small cracked grain of barley that is cooked and served like rice
fd_0180.why: It is not a cereal grass at all, but the seed of a plant related to spinach and beets.

fd_0181.says: Italian rice dish whose creaminess comes from added heavy cream
fd_0181.why: The creaminess is starch rubbed off the rice by stirring, plus butter and cheese at the end.

fd_0182.says: Short, round Spanish rice grown for paella, cooked without stirring
fd_0182.why: It is an Italian risotto rice, and paella rice such as bomba comes from Spain.

fd_0183.says: Black Italian whole-grain rice with a nutty, chewy bran coat
fd_0183.why: It is a polished white rice with its germ added back, not a black whole-grain rice.

fd_0184.says: Fine, powdery white flour from soft wheat, for cakes
fd_0184.why: It is coarse and yellow, from hard durum wheat, the opposite of soft cake flour.

fd_0185.says: Thin, round dried strands made from flour and water alone
fd_0185.why: They are flat ribbons, classically fresh and made with egg.

fd_0186.says: Long, slender Italian rice cooked like pilaf so the grains stay apart
fd_0186.why: It is short and plump, bred to release starch and turn creamy, not stay separate.

fd_0187.says: Tiny whole grain harvested from a North African grass
fd_0187.why: It is a pasta, rolled from wheat semolina, not a whole grain.

fd_0188.says: An ancient grain species of its own, with no relation to wheat at all
fd_0188.why: It is ordinary wheat, usually durum, just harvested green and roasted.

fd_0189.says: Dark whole-grain Asian paddy grain, with the bran layer left on
fd_0189.why: It is not an Asian grain or even true rice; it is a North American water grass.

fd_0194.says: Rich egg-yolk dough stamped into tiny domes with a round cutter
fd_0194.why: It is semolina and water dough, dragged by knife and shaped over a thumb.

fd_0195.says: Melted garlic butter whisked with lemon juice for dipping
fd_0195.why: It is made with olive oil beaten into garlic, not melted butter, and served cool.

fd_0196.says: Brown pan sauce of red wine and shallots for grilled steak
fd_0196.why: It is a pale yellow egg yolk and butter sauce; red wine and shallot is bordelaise.

fd_0197.says: Cold sauce of whipped cream, mustard and lemon for fish
fd_0197.why: It is served warm and built from egg yolks and melted butter, not cream.

fd_0198.says: Clear broth set firm with gelatin and sliced cold
fd_0198.why: That is an aspic; this is fat and water held as droplets, not a set gel.

fd_0199.says: Light sauce used only for beef, the dip for a French dip sandwich
fd_0199.why: It comes from any roast, and lamb and chicken jus are as common as beef.

fd_0200.says: Creamy dressing of mayonnaise, buttermilk and fresh herbs
fd_0200.why: It is oil whisked with vinegar; mayonnaise and buttermilk describe ranch.

fd_0201.says: Sweet red cocktail sauce of ketchup and horseradish
fd_0201.why: It is thin, sharp and clear, made with vinegar and shallot, not ketchup.

fd_0202.says: Balsamic vinegar simmered down on its own until thick
fd_0202.why: It starts from caramelized sugar, and any vinegar can be used, not only balsamic.

fd_0204.says: Light clear soup made by thinning a meat stock down with water
fd_0204.why: It is stronger than the stock it starts from, clarified with egg whites, never thinned.

fd_0205.says: Plain melted butter spooned over fish as it comes out of the pan
fd_0205.why: Melted butter separates into fat and water. This is a creamy emulsion built on a reduction.

fd_0206.says: Half-strength stock thinned with water for a lighter pan sauce
fd_0206.why: Half refers to reducing it by half, which makes it stronger, not weaker.

fd_0208.says: Rich sauce of reduced heavy cream and melted grated parmesan
fd_0208.why: It is milk thickened with cooked butter and flour, not reduced cream and cheese.

fd_0210.says: Smooth blended cilantro and lime sauce spooned over tacos
fd_0210.why: The classic is parsley, oregano and vinegar, chopped, not cilantro and lime.

fd_0212.says: Warm basil cream sauce thickened with butter and flour for pasta
fd_0212.why: It is served raw, and its body comes from cheese, nuts and oil.

fd_0213.says: Fresh raw salsa of chopped tomato, onion, green chile and cilantro
fd_0213.why: It is ground from dried peppers, roasted tomato, nuts and bread, not chopped raw.

fd_0215.says: Chinese sweet and sour sauce of pineapple, ketchup and cornstarch
fd_0215.why: It is Italian, built on vinegar with sugar or honey, often with raisins and onion.

fd_0217.says: Beef ground coarse, pressed into a patty and seared rare on the flat top
fd_0217.why: It is never cooked: the meat is served raw, cut by knife and never ground.

fd_0218.says: Folded French egg dish cooked fast in a hot pan and left soft inside
fd_0218.why: It is cooked slowly and served flat and open, never folded. The fast folded dish is an omelette.

fd_0219.says: Meat stew cooked fast over high heat and served thin and brothy
fd_0219.why: A ragout simmers low and slow until its sauce reduces thick, never fast and brothy.

fd_0221.says: Seafood fully cooked by the lime, so it is no longer raw fish
fd_0221.why: Acid firms and whitens the flesh but does not heat it, so the fish is still raw.

fd_0223.says: Thin slices of beef simmered at the table in a sweet soy broth
fd_0223.why: That is sukiyaki. This is seared hot for seconds, left raw inside and sliced.

fd_0225.says: Any dish smothered in cheese, since the word itself means melted cheese
fd_0225.why: The word means the browned crust on top. Cheese is common, but it is not what makes a dish a gratin.

fd_0228.says: Cold loaf of poached poultry set in its own jelly, served in slices
fd_0228.why: That is a galantine. A ballotine is not set in jelly and is often served hot.

fd_0230.says: Thick, creamy seafood soup with potato, thickened with cream
fd_0230.why: It is a thin saffron broth with pieces of fish, served with bread and rouille. The thick creamy soup is a chowder.

fd_0231.says: Fish wrapped in pastry dough and baked until the crust is golden
fd_0231.why: The wrap is paper, not pastry, and it is never eaten.

fd_0232.says: Fish gently poached in white wine, then coated in a creamy mushroom sauce
fd_0232.why: It is floured and pan-fried in butter, and the sauce is browned butter and lemon, not cream.

fd_0233.says: Fish pressed into a crust of finely ground almond flour, then baked golden
fd_0233.why: The almonds are sliced and toasted, spooned over pan-fried fish, not ground into a baked crust.

fd_0234.says: Thin French pancakes folded around sugar, fruit or chocolate
fd_0234.why: They are fried puffs of yeast dough, not pancakes cooked flat on a griddle.

fd_0235.says: Flaky crescent roll built from many thin layers of butter and dough
fd_0235.why: Its butter is kneaded into the dough, so it is soft and cakey, not flaky and layered.

fd_0236.says: Thin, crisp flatbread topped with tomato sauce and melted cheese
fd_0236.why: It is thick and soft, usually dressed with just oil, salt and herbs rather than sauce and cheese.

fd_0237.says: Bread made sour by mixing vinegar or buttermilk into the dough
fd_0237.why: The sourness comes from fermentation by the starter's bacteria, not from anything poured in.

fd_0238.says: Crisp rolled wafer of almond and butter, curled while still warm
fd_0238.why: It is a pair of smooth, domed almond shells joined by a filling.

fd_0239.says: Two little sponge cakes sandwiched together with cream or jam
fd_0239.why: It is a single mound of coconut and egg white, not a filled sandwich of any kind.

fd_0240.says: Whole eggs and flour whipped into a light sponge, baked in a tall pan
fd_0240.why: It is whites whipped with sugar into an airy foam, not a whole-egg flour batter.

fd_0241.says: Deep dish of fruit baked under a lid of pastry and served warm
fd_0241.why: It has no lid. It is a shallow open shell, filled, with straight sides and a thin crust.

fd_0242.says: Crusty Mexican sandwich roll stuffed with meat, beans and avocado
fd_0242.why: That is a torta, a sandwich. A torte is a dense European cake.

fd_0244.says: Paper-thin stretched sheets brushed with butter, as in baklava
fd_0244.why: That is phyllo. This is one dough folded around a block of butter.

fd_0245.says: Thin French pancake folded around fruit and cream at the table
fd_0245.why: That is a crepe. This is baked in a dish as one thick, custardy cake.

fd_0247.says: Russian honey cake of many thin layers stacked with sour cream
fd_0247.why: The ballerina was Russian, but the dessert is a meringue from Australia or New Zealand.

fd_0248.says: Eggs cooked in a pan and folded over a filling, often with cheese
fd_0248.why: That is an omelette. This is baked in a deep dish and rises on whipped whites.

fd_0249.says: Sweet sauce of butter, sugar and cream cooked until amber and toffee-like
fd_0249.why: That is caramel sauce. This one is yolks and milk, pale and vanilla-scented, never cooked to color.

fd_0250.says: Milk pudding thickened only with cornstarch, cooked quickly to a boil
fd_0250.why: What defines it is egg setting the milk or cream. Starch is optional, and boiling would curdle a plain one.

fd_0251.says: Chocolate melted and cooled with care so it sets shiny and snaps
fd_0251.why: That is tempered chocolate, which is chocolate alone. This is chocolate melted into cream, and it never snaps.

fd_0252.says: Dense dessert of cream and yolks, baked and chilled, then cut in slices
fd_0252.why: It is never baked. It is set by chilling, and its whole point is the air folded into it.

fd_0254.says: Italian cream and yolk dessert baked slowly in a water bath
fd_0254.why: It is never baked. Warm cream is set with gelatin as it chills in the fridge.

fd_0256.says: Italian frozen dessert made richer than ice cream with extra cream and yolks
fd_0256.why: It runs the other way. It leans on milk and is lower in fat than ice cream, and dense from less air.

fd_0257.says: Shaved block of plain frozen water topped with flavored syrup
fd_0257.why: The flavor is frozen into the syrup from the start, not poured over plain ice.

fd_0259.says: Frozen fruit yogurt churned smooth and served as a light scoop
fd_0259.why: It is a fruit and sugar syrup base churned smooth, not a yogurt base.

fd_0260.says: Lean frozen milk and sugar, churned slow and denser than gelato
fd_0260.why: Backwards. It holds more butterfat and more air than gelato, so it is richer and lighter.

fd_0261.says: Half-melted scoop of gelato served soft on a warmed plate
fd_0261.why: It is a frozen mousse sliced from a mold, soft because of air, not because it melted.

fd_0262.says: Baked custard turned out onto a plate with a runny caramel sauce
fd_0262.why: That is flan. This stays in its dish with a hard, torched sugar crust.

fd_0264.says: Whipped butter and sugar frosting spread over the tops of cakes
fd_0264.why: It is a cooked custard of milk and yolks set with starch, not a butter frosting.

fd_0265.says: Cooked vanilla custard lightened with whipped cream to fill cakes
fd_0265.why: It is simply cream whipped with sugar and vanilla, with nothing cooked into it.

fd_0266.says: Red wine vinegar cooked down with sugar until thick and sweet
fd_0266.why: It is built on cooked grape must, and the aged kind thickens in barrels, not with sugar.

fd_0267.says: Sweet fortified wine from the vineyards of eastern France
fd_0267.why: It comes from the far south, on the Mediterranean beside the Spanish border.

fd_0268.says: Aged grape vinegar thickened and sweetened for drizzling
fd_0268.why: It is never soured into vinegar. It is sweet grape must, simply cooked down.

fd_0269.says: Korean cabbage quick-pickled in vinegar and sugar, served cold
fd_0269.why: No vinegar goes in. Its sour comes from days of fermentation by lactic bacteria.

fd_0271.says: Smooth orange jelly made from juice alone, strained of peel
fd_0271.why: The peel is the point: shreds of it run through the preserve and give its bitter edge.

fd_0272.says: Salted Spanish cooking wine used to deglaze a pan sauce
fd_0272.why: It is a true vinegar, soured and then aged in oak, not a salted wine for cooking.

fd_0273.says: Young white wine left to sour into a light, pale vinegar
fd_0273.why: It is never fermented. It is fresh juice from unripe grapes, bottled as it is.

fd_0274.says: Sweet yellow mustard whisked with honey and served as a dipping sauce
fd_0274.why: It is candied fruit in syrup, with mustard only as a hidden heat.

fd_0275.says: Thick curry gravy of slow-cooked meat, spooned over steamed rice
fd_0275.why: It is a relish served on the side, not a curry or a gravy.

fd_0276.says: Clear fruit juice set firm with gelatin, then cut into little cubes
fd_0276.why: It is cooked whole or crushed fruit set by its own pectin, not juice and gelatin.

fd_0277.says: Citrus peel simmered in sugar syrup, then rolled in sugar and dried
fd_0277.why: It is cured in salt, not sugar, and tastes salty and savory, not candied.

fd_0278.says: Small green peppercorns pickled in brine to add a mild, fruity heat
fd_0278.why: They are flower buds of a shrub, not peppercorns, and bring salt and tang, not heat.

fd_0279.says: Sweet pickle sliced into thin coins with onion, made for sandwiches
fd_0279.why: It is a whole, tiny, sour pickle, not a sweet sliced one.

fd_0280.says: Clear Japanese broth steeped from kelp and dried bonito flakes
fd_0280.why: That is dashi, the broth it is stirred into, not the paste itself.

fd_0281.says: Dark liquid brewed from soybeans and wheat, used for dipping sushi
fd_0281.why: That is soy sauce. This is made from salted, fermented anchovies.

fd_0282.says: Fermented chili and soybean paste, sweet and sticky, from Korea
fd_0282.why: That is gochujang. This is unfermented, just dried chilies pounded with garlic and spices.

fd_0283.says: Always fiery hot ground chili, a Spanish version of cayenne
fd_0283.why: Most of it is sweet or bittersweet. Only the hot style carries real heat.

fd_0284.says: Fine seasoning grain dissolved into a sauce at the end of cooking
fd_0284.why: It is coarse and goes on dry, on top, so it stays crunchy instead of dissolving.
